finding: For a four-MOQLS8 family with THREE actual classical members, a nonclassical member cannot have an intrinsic C6 component of real projector span <=12. This is conditional on the stated q1 classical-mate hypotheses, NOT an unrestricted no-C6 theorem. The only imported theorem is adopted GAP3.
proof_outline: At a selected component cell the classical companions and row/column supply five actual net lines meeting pairwise only there. The star >=5I, two-plane <=3 rays and three-space <=6 rays are derived from physical ONBs. At b<=12, a connected5 star-basis pivot is ruled out: it forces sigma=9,Ldim2, and every connected5 unitary has a row or column with at most one zero; its diagonal-pencil ray cone plus a direction orthogonal to the cross image contradicts star>=5. 4+1 pivots are ruled out by the 2-fold common-star spanning lemma and a shared-axis multiplicity contradiction. With no 2-block allowed, the five net lines force a 3+1+1 pivot. Cross rank0/1 and common-A/common-B rank2 are excluded by the star bound and 3-space cap. The remaining independent-rank2 pencil has six pure-A rays (two 3-ONBs with exactly one cross zero, giving one unique ray in each), two pure-B axes and two mixed two-planes. Any five-ONB with mixed rays must use an orthopair in each mixed plane, those planes must be orthogonal, and it must include the same pure-A ray t. The two unmixed pivot lines cannot repeat (each has its unique ray); mixed lines can occur at most twice because t occurs on a pivot line and GAP3 caps multiplicity at3. At most4 lines contradict the actual5-net.
